headline: Angara Urges Stronger Student Support as Gun-Safety Debate Grows After Zamboanga Shooting
seoTitle: Angara Urges Stronger Student Support After Zamboanga School Shooting | FMB News
seoDescription: Education Secretary Sonny Angara urged stronger school-community support for students after visiting Ateneo de Zamboanga, as authorities and lawmakers continue debating firearm safety and accountability.
deck: Angara said preventing school violence requires more than physical security, while investigators and policymakers continue examining firearm access and accountability after the fatal attack.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: A shooting at a school attached to Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City on August 18 left two students dead, including the suspected shooter, and two other people injured. Authorities continue to investigate how the student obtained firearms belonging to his father, a Bureau of Customs official.

Reuters reported on August 19 that Education Secretary Sonny Angara visited Ateneo de Zamboanga University and said preventing school violence requires more than fences, CCTV cameras, metal detectors and other physical security measures. He emphasized the importance of school communities reaching out to students and said even small interventions can have a significant impact on young people.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The same Reuters report said Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla urged lawmakers to stiffen penalties for gun owners whose firearms are accessed by minors and to revisit laws governing loose firearms. Republic Act No. 10591 already requires licensed firearm owners to keep firearms in a vault, locked container or under other security measures.

FMB News is not presenting the newsroom email's broader claim that Angara ordered a nationwide mental-health overhaul, nor its separate claim about mandatory biometric firearm storage, as verified facts because those specific measures were not independently corroborated in the sources reviewed for this update.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The case has widened the policy discussion beyond physical campus security to include how schools identify distress, how communities support students, how firearms are secured at home, and what accountability applies when a licensed weapon is accessed by a minor. Those questions should remain distinct from the still-open investigation into motive and firearm access in this specific case.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal PNP and Bureau of Customs findings on firearm access and chain of custody, any concrete DepEd measures on student support and school safety, and any bill or officially released amendment proposal that would change firearm-owner liability or storage requirements under Republic Act No. 10591.
